close_reason: Added explicit performance contract on JmapBackend::account_exists doc — sub-millisecond, in-memory cache or local indexed lookup, anti-pattern is remote DB round-trip per call. Dispatcher-layer caching is workspace-architectural and out of scope.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:808-817 — JmapBackend::account_exists is
documented as:

> Return `true` if the given account exists in this backend.
>
> Handlers call this at the start of each method to return
> `accountNotFound` (RFC 8620 §3.6.2) rather than surfacing
> the wrong error when `accountId` is unknown.

The doc tells implementors WHERE the method is called (start of each
method) but not WHAT the implementor must guarantee. handlers.rs
confirms the pattern: handle_get, handle_changes, handle_query,
handle_query_changes all open with:

    if !backend.account_exists(caller, &account_id).await.map_err(...)?

That is FOUR backend roundtrips per typical /get + /changes + /query
+ /queryChanges sequence (a single client batch). Extension *-server
crates inherit the pattern.

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That a slow account_exists is "fine because it's just an
   existence check". A backend that does a Postgres SELECT or a
   network RPC for every check multiplies every JMAP method call's
   latency by one extra round-trip — silently.

2. That cache invalidation around account_exists is the
   backend's responsibility. The kit doesn't cache. Every call
   site re-asks. The doc doesn't tell the implementor "you should
   probably cache this".

3. That the perf cost is bounded. A batch of 16 method calls (the
   conventional max_calls in jmap-server) produces 16 round-trips
   in addition to the actual data fetch.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- A backend implementor naively writes account_exists to do a
  full database round-trip and ships. Production latency at scale
  doubles. The cause is not obviously in the backend impl — the
  call is invisible from the handler-author's perspective.
- An audit or perf review of an extension *-server crate finds
  the issue six months in.
- A future contributor adds caching at the wrong layer (handler
  side, with cache-invalidation timing wrong against the
  backend's truth) and introduces a stale-cache bug.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):

- Document the perf contract on the trait method:
  "Implementations SHOULD return in sub-millisecond time
  (in-memory cache, indexed primary key, etc.). A naive remote
  round-trip is incorrect — handlers call this at the start of
  every method invocation."

- Cache at the dispatcher layer: store the verified accountId set
  for the duration of a single dispatch call, so 16 method calls
  in a batch hit the backend at most once per unique accountId.
  Workspace-architectural decision (touches Dispatcher state
  during a single dispatch call).

- Push the check into the handler-side helper that handlers
  already use (extract_account_id) — but extract_account_id is
  sync and account_exists is async; not a drop-in fix.

The doc-only fix is right for the current review. The dispatcher-
layer caching is the structural fix and is a workspace-architectural
decision.
title: JmapBackend::account_exists is called per-method-call but perf contract is undocumented
